planHostWidth-editorVue.scope: applyHostPageState is the open/tab-switch funnel: an immediate watcher on the active tab id (covering boot via the app.vue v-if mount, switches, and close-to-unmount), seq-guarded per tab exactly like applyStoredTableLayouts. It loads the document's pageWidths entry through util/pageWidthStore.loadPageWidthFor (prune + cap inside the store util; a falsy pathname — untitled/guide tabs — short-circuits without any IO), applies the document tier through resolveEffectiveWidth -> applyEditorWidth (one inline --editorAreaWidth write; the canvas clamp never writes the store, corner C-2), and for entry-less documents calls clearAppliedEditorWidth so the legacy global writer (theme.js setEditorWidth via the shipped editorLineWidth watcher) owns the variable again — exactly one writer, the panel's hand-off semantics.
planHostWidth-editorVue.canvasReapply: reapplyHostWidthFromCache + a watcher on [window resize, showSideBar, sideBarWidth]: the cached entry re-resolves onto the canvas — one custom-property write per relayout event, never a content re-render, no store IO on the tick (corner C-3; the sidebar drag commits its width on mouseup, the same layout-store model the panel uses). A 150 ms trailing freshen re-reads the entry once per burst, and an editorLineWidth change schedules the same freshen — so the panel's direct store writes can never leave the host cache stale.
planHostWidth-editorVue.panelAnnouncement: handleDocumentPageStateChanged: the panel announces its writes on the renderer bus (mt::document-page-state-changed, emitted by pageTab.persistAndApply/onReset and viewTab.saveEntry); the host re-reads the entry so a fresh pin or width reaches the surface without waiting for a tab switch; announcements for other documents are ignored.
planHostWidth-editorVue.cleanup: onBeforeUnmount (the last document closed — app.vue v-if unmounts the editor column): the pending freshen dies, the resize listener and the bus handler come off, the inline pipeline value is cleared (the legacy writer owns the variable for the welcome screen) and a pinned surface theme is restored — the C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY cleanup discipline.

planRenameMove-editorStore.scope: RENAME and RENAME_IF_NEEDED both call util/pageWidthStore.movePageWidthEntry — fire-and-forget with the BLOCK_PAGE_WIDTH_MOVE_FAILED marker, mirroring the moveTableLayoutsEntry/moveFilePositionsEntry hooks line-for-line — so a document's remembered width and the pinned theme inside the same entry follow renames from both the title-bar card and the sidebar.

planPinnedTheme-R4.scope: applyDocumentSurfaceTheme applies entry.themeOverride to the document surface through addThemeStyle, with syncDiagramClassification keeping the muya mermaid/vega options on the APPLIED theme (the shipped watch(theme) /dark/i branch — the global preference is never rewritten). A global theme cycle (title bar, Settings, Auto resolution, cross-window echo) while a pin is on the surface re-asserts the pin and never touches the stored entry (only the View tab writes themeOverride). Switching to an unpinned document, or unmount, restores the Auto-aware global theme (resolveAutoTheme under followSystemTheme). The boot funnel runs at setup AND once at the end of onMounted: the setup pass can land before the Muya instance exists (Vue flushes mounted hooks on a microtask that can lose to the funnel's first await), so the second pass guarantees the classification sync; the duplicate apply costs one extra property write + one store read at boot.

T-007-tableFit.scope: The R-9 algorithm, pure maths separated from DOM measurement: measureColumnExtents (three-phase clone measurement INSIDE the table's own scroll wrapper so the theme CSS chain styles the clone — max-content (nowrap), min-content (longest unbreakable token), wrappedMin (overflow-wrap: anywhere); header + first FIT_MEASURE_ROW_LIMIT=50 rows; zero geometry -> null like every muya measurer); planTableFit decision order (distribute when sum(minima) fits -> wrap-anywhere fallback -> honest minimal-size scroll degradation with the exact overflowPx); distributeIntoFrame (water-filling proportional to the remaining slack, capped at maxContent, the leftover after all caps split EVENLY — the Word AutoFit Window behaviour, so a frame wider than max-content still fills); snapWidthsToInt (largest-remainder integer snap summing exactly to the frame); applyRatiosToWidth/ratiosFromWidths (the T-008 ratio re-application with minima floors and donor rebalancing).
T-007-tableFit.measuredBehaviour: On the plan's C-7 fixtures in real Chromium: a 6-column table fits its frame and the wrapper never scrolls; a 300-char token wraps (kind 'wrap') instead of scrolling; the 30-column fixture degrades with the badge reporting the exact px ('Does not fit by 1943 px'). Measured floor discovery: the shipped .ag-cell-content { min-width: 4em } floors every cell at ~90px, so column minima are honest and large — the algorithm reports degradation exactly when the editor genuinely cannot render smaller.

T-007-threeModeModel.scope: Auto = content-sized (the C-39 wrapper-scroll behaviour, GitHub model — the pre-C-65 default restored). Fit page: the frame is the wrapper's CONTENT box (the text column minus the 11px row-bar padding); Full width: the breakout viewport (container minus gutter). modeOf() resolves the explicit session choice (modes map) over the tri-state tableFullWidthDefault option ('fit'/'full', else 'auto' — the legacy fake-fit boolean default maps to Auto, retiring the auto-expansion). The fit funnel: applyTableLayout per table (render reconcile + refitAll via one ResizeObserver over container+figures, debounced 200ms + rAF per plan review F7; jsdom degrades to render-time only), extents cached per identity/structure/font-size, degradation dataset (figure[data-degrade-overflow]) driving the caption badge, wrap-anywhere class for the wrap plan. sanitizePersistedEntries v2 with the IDEMPOTENT migration: legacy fullWidth -> mode 'full', legacy fit -> mode 'fit' (owner gate no.4), booleans never written again; rememberTableColumnSizes=false gates persist() and adoption. Column drags in Fit/Full fix the dragged column and re-fit the remainder into the frame (the table never leaves it); zero-move drags no longer write. reconcileAfterRender keeps the column-count reconcile (a new column takes its measured content share and ratios renormalise, T-008).

T-008.scope: Schema v2: entries { widths, manual, mode?, ratios?, tableWidth? }; the store reads v1 or v2 and normalizes to version 2 (EMPTY_STORE v2); sanitizeEntry delegates to tableLayoutRatios.migrateTableEntry (shared normative rules, husks drop); muya drags write widths + ratios + tableWidth; window/zoom/page-width/mode-switch re-applies ratios through applyRatiosToWidth (floors at the measured minima, rebalances over donors, integer-snaps to the frame); Auto keeps ratios stored but unapplied (no mode field); the 30-file cap, prune and rename move unchanged. editor.vue passes the two Tables-tab preferences into muya options (tableFullWidthDefault tri-state, rememberTableColumnSizes) with two watchers (mode default re-renders, the gate does not).

T-009.scope: The toolbar toggle becomes the honest three-mode segment (Auto / Fit page / Full width buttons with dataset.tableMode + setMode action; the vnode carries the Full fact, updateToolbarModeDom corrects Fit/Auto before paint). The shipped C-39 6px col-resize handles are untouched (parity pinned: cursor + hover hairline verified in e2e). Drag chips: one '% · N px' chip per column above the table during a drag, fading out after release (CHIPS_FADE_MS 700).
